e.text: A3 leads at 24.1% vs benchmark 6.5%; asking the Critic how to push A3 and A1 further.

e.note: Reading results for A3, A1

critique.summary: Both plans beat the benchmark by more than 3x (A3 24.1% at $485 per point vs benchmark 6.5% at $1812), driven by the Nasty Gal drop, early host-read podcasts and Lower West Side/Bridgeport partners that feed strong word of mouth. What is not working: 41 days of citywide social in A1 costs $7380 for 15.5% of adoption, several $300 partners in New City, Little Village and Bridgeport earn under 1.2%, and Luxury streetwear and R&B (East Garfield Park, the core R&B crowd) lags at about 18–19% with no seeding.

findings.finding: Highest mean reach (24.1%) and strongest 10th percentile (21.9%) at $485 per point, with the Nasty Gal drop (11.1% for $2000) and two host-read ads (7.0% and 6.0% for $3400 each) doing the heavy lifting and word of mouth at 59.5%.
My Second Home in New City earned just 0.7%, and Plaza Garibaldi in Little Village and National Museum of Mexican Art each earned 1.2% for $300, the weakest returns in the plan.
Reach of 22.6% (10th percentile 20.2%) at $521 per point trails A3, because 41 days of social cost $7380 for 15.5% of adoption, worse per dollar than A3's 6-day $1080 burst (2.3%) plus podcasts.

Bridgeport partners One City Tap (1.0%), Zhou B Art Center (0.9%) and Co-Prosperity (0.9%) are the weakest, while Lower West Side galleries Vault Gallerie and NYCH earn 1.8% each; Indie rock and Drag Race reaches 33.0%, but Latin pop and shooter games reaches only 17.7%.
Reach of 6.5% at $1812 per point, with broad social taking $6660 for 22.2% of credit, confirms that taste-targeted seeding is far more efficient.

changes.change: Start from A3 and drop My Second Home (New City). Use the $300 toward a seed in East Garfield Park, the unseeded R&B and streetwear zone, on day 0.
changes.why: A $300 partner returning 0.7% is the worst buy in the plan, and Luxury streetwear and R&B sits at only 18.8% with no seeds in its hot zone.

changes.change: Add Lower West Side galleries NYCH Gallery (partner:C2630CA4…) from A1 to A3 at day 0, funded by trimming A3's social:city from 6 days to 3 days.
changes.why: NYCH earned 1.8% for $300 in A1, while A3's social earned 2.3% for $1080.

changes.change: Keep both host-read podcasts on days 0 and 2 and the Nasty Gal collab from day 0 for 41 days. Do not adopt A1's 41-day social:city.
changes.why: The podcasts and collab deliver 24.1% of A3's adoption combined, while long-run social cost $7380 for 15.5% in A1.

changes.change: Exclude low-earning Bridgeport partners Zhou B Art Center and Co-Prosperity from any A1-style variant.
changes.why: Each was credited with only 0.9% for $300.

What is not working: 41 days of citywide social in A1 costs $7380 for 15.5% of adoption, several $300 partners in New City, Little Village and Bridgeport earn under 1.2%, and Luxury streetwear and R&B (East Garfield Park, the core R&B crowd) lags at about 18–19% with no seeding.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B2

plan.headline: Grassroots Pilsen-area partners plus Nasty Gal drop: ~25% simulated reach, 3.8x benchmark
plan.summary: The bet is to build adoption inside the neighbourhoods themselves, with nine local partners across Pilsen, Bridgeport, New City and Little Village, a Nasty Gal co-branded drop, one early Insanely Chill read and three weeks of fit-weighted citywide social. Qloo taste data shows these places and brands over-index with Kali Uchis, Omar Apollo and Cuco fans, with affinities of 0.82–0.97. In a simulation built on that data, the plan reaches about 24.7% of the natural audience (range 22.5%–27.2%), about 3.8x the 6.5% benchmark, at $481 per point of reach versus $1812, with word of mouth driving 58.7% of adoption; this is a projection, not a guarantee.

weeks.label: Week 1 (days 41–35 before launch)
items: Day 41: run the host-read ad on Insanely Chill w/ Cody Ko.
Day 41: launch the Nasty Gal co-branded drop, which stays live until launch.
Day 41: start fit-weighted citywide social ads for a 21-day run.
Place posters, flyers and counter cards at all nine partners, starting with the National Museum of Mexican Art, Vault Gallerie and NYCH Gallery.

weeks.label: Weeks 2–3 (days 34–21 before launch)
items: Keep social running and refresh creative mid-run using the Nasty Gal drop imagery.
Check every partner's display and restock flyers, especially in Little Village and New City.
Ask partners to repost so word of mouth stays visible.

weeks.label: Weeks 4–5 (days 20–7 before launch)
items: Social ends at day 20, so word of mouth and partners carry the push from here.
Push the Nasty Gal drop reminder and share a preview track at the galleries and the gym.

weeks.label: Launch week (days 6–0)
items: Run a final restock and 'last tickets' signage at all partners.
Close out the Nasty Gal drop with show-night messaging.
